patient_profile.name: Patient F (represented by mother)
history: born full term, no history of asthma or reactive airway disease
up to date on all childhood vaccinations
patient_profile.presenting_complaint: sudden onset of a loud 'barking' cough, hoarse cry, and a squeaking sound when breathing in that started 4 hours ago

hidden_ground_truth.stage: Moderate croup (stridor at rest with mild chest retractions, but no respiratory distress/hypoxia)
hidden_ground_truth.correct_first_line_treatment: Single dose of oral or intramuscular dexamethasone (0.6 mg/kg). If stridor at rest is persistent or severe, nebulized racemic epinephrine should be given. Keep the child calm to avoid worsening airway obstruction.
critical_early_tests: clinical assessment of croup severity (e.g. Westley Croup Score)
red_herrings: mother mentions he was playing with small Lego blocks earlier today, raising concern for foreign body inhalation (though the classic prodrome and barky cough point strongly to croup)

initial: loud 'seal-like' barking cough that woke him up from sleep
squeaking noise when breathing in (inspiratory stridor), especially when crying or agitated
mild runny nose and low-grade fever for the last 2 days

on_direct_questioning.choking_episode: No, I didn't see him choke or gasp suddenly while playing with the Legos. He had a runny nose for two days before this barking cough started tonight.
on_direct_questioning.drooling_or_swallowing: No, he is not drooling. He was able to swallow water and juice without any trouble earlier this evening.
on_direct_questioning.color_change: No, his face and lips have stayed their normal pink color, he doesn't look blue or pale.

physical_exam.general: Alert, sitting on mother's lap, looks mildly anxious, breathing through mouth
physical_exam.throat: mildly red, no swelling of the tonsils, no drooling
physical_exam.respiratory: audible inspiratory stridor at rest, mild subcostal and intercostal retractions, lungs otherwise clear with equal breath sounds, no wheezing or rales
physical_exam.skin: no cyanosis, warm and well perfused

lab_results.neck_xray: AP view of neck shows symmetric subglottic narrowing, also known as the 'steeple sign'; lateral view shows a normal-appearing epiglottis

progression_rules.if_untreated_or_delayed: airway swelling can worsen, leading to increased work of breathing, severe retractions, fatigue, and potential hypoxia requiring intensive monitoring
progression_rules.if_correct_treatment: rapid clinical improvement with resolution of stridor at rest and decreased work of breathing within 1-2 hours after corticosteroids/epinephrine
progression_rules.if_incorrect_or_unnecessary_treatment: e.g. attempting to start an IV or draw blood unnecessarily causes significant agitation and distress, which physically worsens subglottic narrowing and stridor; antibiotics are useless because croup is viral
progression_rules.if_unnecessary_invasive_test_ordered: note the added distress/agitation to the child in the scoring, and simulate normal results
